column2: Work program: wood cutting; at the farm, bedding, corn, fences, clearing and plowing between the two big fields; insulation under the Studies Building; grounds of the magnesium pilot plant; lending of shop tools restored, shop cleaned; six pounds of mica; coal
Faculty and Student Officers: the whole session devoted to Black Mountain College, chaired by Charles Lindsley, who is to speak about it at the University of Virginia
Arrival of Dr. and Mrs. Edwin G. Boring, Molly Boring's parents, for a short visit
Betty Kelley reads and discusses the outline of her children's play before the executive board of the Asheville Children's Theatre and schoolteachers
Walter Rubsamen (UCLA): talk on “Music in Nazi Germany and Soviet Russia,” in place of the Saturday concert or play
Clark Foreman leaves for Atlanta, for the founding meeting of the Southern Regional Conference
Work program: rain and mud; unloading coal; pit for the gasoline tank at the Shop Road fork; some wood cutting, Ross Penley saws the cords; mica mine closed until spring; seasonal work at the farm
Two carloads of coal arrive, unloaded in record time despite the rain (empty by Saturday morning)
Arrival of Miss Rita E. Foley, the new secretary, who will work mainly with Bob Wunsch
Diomedes de Pereyra, Bolivian novelist and essayist, arrives for a few days

Work program: barn loft filled with hay; wood cutting and clearing nearly finished; framing of the steers' shed; fence of the old hog pen taken down; mailing lists updated at the office; mica trimming
Josef Albers leaves to prepare the summer Art Institute at Lake Eden
Danny Deaver graduates in class 44-3 of the advanced navigation school at Ellington Field, commissioned a lieutenant

Work program: with the two Gibsons, rapid clearing (sixty cords of wood ready); sawing and hauling; floor and framing of the steers' shed; sorting mica; inventory of supplies and equipment (Bas Allen)
Death of Ann (Annarrah) Kurtz after several months of illness
The Social Survey class and Herbert Miller have supper with Father Greenwood and parishioners at the rectory of St. James Episcopal Church
Marriage of Mary Aydelette Rice, daughter of Mrs. Nell Aydelette Rice, to Roger Duryea Marshall
Herbert Miller helps set up a program of public speaking courses with and for convalescent officers
Marriage of Avis Rebecca Belt and Lieutenant Boonyong Nikrodhonandra (Free Thai Unit)
Musical evening at the Lowinskys' (Black Dwarf): Bach and Couperin
First meeting of the Campaign Publicity Committee: articles by faculty members (Jalowetz on Schoenberg at seventy), publicity for the summer institutes, a series of broadcasts on WWNC
Paul Radin leaves for New York
Gisela Kronenberg starts as a special student at the Lewis Institute
Work program during the Interlude: wood, sorting mica, farm (cleaning, manure, bedding); steers' shed boarded; dining hall floor washed; debris of the Service Building sorted
Bruno Piscitello is sent to Lubbock Field; Aurora Cassotta Piscitello leaves on Thursday for Tucson
Trudi Straus returns from Raleigh, where she played in the concerts of the North Carolina Symphony Orchestra
Wide World Photos distributes to subscribing newspapers a series of eleven photographs of Black Mountain College, for release from Sunday, March 12

Work program: more clearing, brush fires, logs to the sawmill for the last wall of the shed; manure on the fields; Josef Albers and students move the big hydrangea near the library; set for “Outward Bound” begun; 13 and a half pounds of mica for Asheville; copying lists for the survey of the town of Black Mountain
Visitors of the week: Pete Hill and Joy Corbett, a friend of Ati Gropius (Max Dehn speaks on Thursday)
Bob Marden resumes classes at the AACS school, transferred to Scott Field
Bill Berry graduates in class 44-4 of the navigation school at Selman Field, commissioned a lieutenant
Arrival of Dr. George N. Redd (Fisk University) and two Fisk science students, Robert Lee and Robert Powell
The text of the college bulletin on the Summer Music Institute goes to Biltmore Press

Work program: steers' shed finished (with Mundy and Walter), a study fitted out in the Studies Building, furniture for “Outward Bound”; manure and two acres cleared above the mica mine; logs to the Morris sawmill; new full-time kitchen crew; hauling crew reduced to three
Social half hour after dinner: Emil Willimetz calls the square dance figures
Lieutenant Bela Martin spends a few hours at Lake Eden
Emil Willimetz, from Camp Shelby, visits the college
Dr. George N. Redd speaks about education and gives his impressions of Black Mountain College
Annual state drama festival at Chapel Hill (March 23-25): Black Mountain College takes part
Dr. Redd, Robert Lee, and Robert Powell leave for Fisk University
The Christian Science Monitor publishes a photo of the Lake Eden farm and a caption on the Community Work Program
The pigs escape; the cows spend their first day on the barley pasture
The detailed bulletins of the Music Institute, the Art Institute, and the Summer School and Work Camp come back from the printer this week
Life publishes a note by Clark Foreman and a photo of Charles Beard, Ted Dreier, and Ati Gropius on a bench in front of the dining hall
Work program: rain; potatoes gathered and seed potatoes cut; corn shelled; posts and holes for a fence around the lower field; manure on the curved field; repairs all over the campus

Visitors of the week: Otis Levy (on his way to a new assignment), Sue Blanchard, then Isabel Cameron and Miss Wagner (from Concord, staying with Ati Gropius), Corporal Hubert Allen, Lorna Pearson (admitted for 1944-45) and her father
Ted and Bobbie Dreier leave for a week's vacation in Florida
Frederic Cohen leaves for New York to see critics and editors about the Summer Music Institute
Jo Starling, a student at the Woman's College in Greensboro, arrives for a short visit with Mary Brett
A son born to Charles and Mrs. Lindsley
Mrs. A. D. Jamieson (Newton Centre), a member of the Advisory Council, arrives for a visit until Wednesday

Mr. and Mrs. George Zabriskie (Durham) visit for the weekend; Zabriskie, a candidate for the position of writing teacher, speaks informally on “Modern Writers” on Saturday evening in Bob Wunsch's office
Fred Wale, of the Rosenwald Fund, and Mrs. Wale arrive for five days
Dora Leiper, a friend of the faculty, and Martine Seligman arrive for a short visit
Election: Mary Brett becomes a student officer in place of Janie Robinson Stone, who steps down to prepare for her graduation
Dora Harrison Diffenderfer starts as an apprentice welder at the Kaiser shipyards
Trudi Straus leaves for Chapel Hill, Greensboro, and Greenville, weekend concerts with the North Carolina Symphony Orchestra
Lieutenant Bela Martin flies in from Green Cove Springs to see Bob Wunsch for two hours in Asheville
Oscar Wilde, “The Importance of Being Earnest” for the A.A.F. rest camp (Bauer, Bray, Dinkowitz, Flax, Gifford, Fred and Nell Goldsmith, Ostrow, Swackhamer); return in a downpour
The heifers, steers, and three dairy heifers go up to the mountain pasture
Paul Radin leaves for Washington on business
Departure of Dora Leiper, Lana Yarash's guest for the past ten days
Mrs. John Carr and her daughter Dorothy (Winchester, Massachusetts), guests of the college until Sunday afternoon
Mr. and Mrs. Morris Mandlebaum, Judy's parents, arrive from Newark for a few days
Mrs. Samuel Pevsner, mother of Marita and Viera, arrives from Washington
Marriage of Nanette Wright and Lieutenant Richard Hastings Wright Jr.
Arrival of Laddie Marshak, a new student, for the spring quarter
Paul Radin returns to the college
Louis Levy leaves after a week's vacation at Lake Eden
After several postponements due to canceled flights, Anne Mangold leaves for Knoxville, where she takes a plane for Mexico City
Dr. and Mrs. Max Shellins arrive for a visit; departure on the afternoon of the 15th
E. R. Goodridge, a friend of Paul Radin, arrives for four days
Lieutenant Bill Hanchett flies a plane from Bainbridge (Georgia) to Fletcher and comes to the college with Lieutenant Converse; visit on Friday evening and Saturday
Bill Hanchett goes back to Georgia

A quarter of an hour before curtain time at Moore General Hospital, Jerry Flax breaks his wrist putting up the set; a makeshift splint lets him play Lane in the first act of “The Importance of Being Earnest”
Departure of Mr. and Mrs. A. D. Stone (Richmond)
W. M. Cole arrives with his secretary Erma Emery for the semiannual audit of the accounts
Miss Eunice Miller, Herbert Miller's sister, arrives for a visit
Jimmy Jamieson leaves, after two weeks at Lake Eden, for the hospital in Brattleboro (Vermont)
The Board of Fellows accepts the resignation of Mrs. Helen Lounsbury and appoints Mrs. Stone, Fred Stone's mother, hostess of the lodges
Clifford Pope arrives from Chicago for five days: mountain excursions, specimens for the Chicago Natural History Museum
Theodore M. Greene (Princeton) and Arthur M. Bannerman, president of Warren Wilson Junior College, come to see Bob Wunsch
Connie Spencer arrives from Washington for five days
Private Robert Marden arrives on furlough from Scott Field; leaves on Thursday for the Greensboro air base
Mrs. Annette Dabney Stone arrives from Richmond to be the college's hostess
Private Dick Brown arrives for part of his furlough from Scott Field
H. B. Adams (Lenoir), Henry Adams's father, visiting
Jascha Klein (St. John's College) arrives for a visit
Sam Brown leaves for Wilton (Connecticut) and a medical appointment in Boston, accompanied part of the way by his brother Dick Brown; back for the Music Institute
Kedric Lynch, Patsy's brother, arrives for a week
Jack Lipsey arrives from Atlanta to prepare his return to Lake Eden in July
John Campbell leaves for the C.P.S. camp at Grottoes (Virginia)
John Chen, a Methodist minister from Nanking (Drew University), and Vladimir Hartman, a Baptist minister, visiting
Robert Marden leaves for his new assignment in Greensboro
William Morse Cole goes back to Concord after the semiannual audit
Mrs. Helen Lounsbury leaves for her summer home in Highlands
Mary Brett leaves for New York, for the wedding of her sister Betty to Will Hamlin
Jack Gifford leaves to work for the summer at the Cape May Playhouse (New Jersey)
At lunch, Bob Wunsch announces a $4000 check received in the morning mail, a gift from Stephen Forbes, a former student
Birth of Ann Hughes, daughter of Mary Hughes Pendergrass
